    // Where the segment crosses the plane, with Parameter in [0, 1] along A -> B.
    // Misses when the segment is parallel to the plane OR both endpoints lie on the
    // same side (the crossing parameter falls outside [0, 1]).
    Intersect(s: Line3D, pl: Plane): PlaneHit3D
    {
        var denom = s.A.Between(s.B).Dot(pl.Normal.Vector);
        var t = 0.0 - pl.SignedDistance(s.A) / denom;
        return denom == 0.0 || t < 0.0 || t > 1.0
            ? (false, s.A, 0.0)
            : (true, s.PointAt(t), t);
    }

    //==
    // # Ray - triangle
    //
    // Moller-Trumbore: solve the ray/triangle system directly for the barycentric
    // pair and the distance, with no precomputed plane
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moller-Trumbore_intersection_algorithm).
    // The determinant is the scalar triple product of the two edge vectors and the
    // ray direction, so it vanishes exactly when the ray is parallel to the
    // triangle's plane. Backfaces are NOT culled: a hit is reported whichever side
    // the ray arrives from.

    // The unnormalized barycentric-and-distance solution of the ray/triangle system,
    // as (determinant, u, v, t). Meaningful only where the determinant is non-zero;
    // the containment and forward-facing tests are TriangleHit's, not this one's.
    MollerTrumbore(r: Ray3D, t: Triangle3D): Number4
    {
        var e1 = t.A.Between(t.B);
        var e2 = t.A.Between(t.C);
        var p = r.Direction.Vector.Cross(e2);
        var det = e1.Dot(p);
        var s = t.A.Between(r.Origin);
        var q = s.Cross(e1);
        return (det, s.Dot(p), r.Direction.Vector.Dot(q), e2.Dot(q));
    }

    // Where the ray strikes the triangle. Misses when the ray is parallel to the
    // triangle's plane, when the crossing point falls outside the triangle, or when
    // it lies behind the ray origin. The reported normal is the triangle's own,
    // flipped when the ray arrives from behind it, so it always opposes the ray.
    // Face is 0 on a hit and -1 on a miss: a lone triangle is its own face 0.
    Raycast(tri: Triangle3D, r: Ray3D): RayHit3D
    {
        var m = MollerTrumbore(r, tri);
        var inv = 1.0 / m.X;
        var u = m.Y * inv;
        var v = m.Z * inv;
        var t = m.W * inv;
        var inside = u >= 0.0 && v >= 0.0 && u + v <= 1.0;
        var n = tri.Normal;
        var facing = n.Vector.Dot(r.Direction.Vector) <= 0.0 ? n : Direction3D(n.Vector.Negative);
        return m.X == 0.0 || !inside || t < 0.0
            ? (false, 0.0, r.Origin, n, FaceIndex(-1), BarycentricCoordinate(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), UvCoordinate(0.0, 0.0))
            : (true, t, r.PointAt(t), facing, FaceIndex(0),
               BarycentricCoordinate(1.0 - u - v, u, v), UvCoordinate(u, v));
    }

    // True when `point` lies on or behind the boundary plane
    // (Dot(Normal, point) <= Distance). Boundary inclusive.
    Contains(h: HalfSpace, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => h.Boundary.SignedDistance(point) <= 0.0;

    // The query point itself when it is inside the half-space, otherwise its
    // projection onto the boundary plane.
    ClosestPoint(h: HalfSpace, point: Point3D): Point3D
        => h.Contains(point) ? point : h.Boundary.ClosestPoint(point);

    // True when `point` lies on or behind the boundary line. Boundary inclusive.
    Contains(h: HalfPlane2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => h.SignedDistance(point) <= 0.0;

    // The query point itself when it is inside the half-plane, otherwise its
    // projection onto the boundary line.
    ClosestPoint(h: HalfPlane2D, point: Point2D): Point2D
        => h.Contains(point)
        ? point
        : point - h.Normal.Vector * h.SignedDistance(point);

    //==
    // # Plane — the former host intrinsics
    //
    // These ten bodies used to be bodiless declarations in
    // `intrinsics-planes.library.plato`, forwarded to `System.Numerics.Plane`.
    // They are ordinary Plato now, so the host contract is one file with no
    // exceptions; the trade is that generated C# no longer routes plane
    // operations through System.Numerics and loses its SIMD acceleration.
    //
    // Two conventions decide the signs below and are stated per body:
    //   * Hesse form is `Dot(Normal, p) = Distance` (this vocabulary), where
    //     System.Numerics uses `Dot(Normal, p) + D = 0`, i.e. `D = -Distance`.
    //   * Matrices multiply a ROW vector on the left, `v' = v M`
    //     (CONVENTIONS.md - Matrices), so `RowN` is the image of basis vector N.

    // A copy of the plane whose normal has unit length, with Distance divided by
    // the same factor so the point set Dot(Normal, p) = Distance is unchanged.
    // The identity when Direction3D's unit invariant holds; the repair path after
    // a non-rigid transform has broken it.
    Normalize(pl: Plane): Plane
    {
        var len = pl.Normal.Vector.Length;
        return (Direction3D(pl.Normal.Vector / len), pl.Distance / len);
    }

    // The plane through three points, facing the side from which the winding
    // point1 -> point2 -> point3 reads counter-clockwise: the normal is the unit
    // cross product (point2 - point1) x (point3 - point1) under the right-hand
    // rule, and Distance is Dot(normal, point1), the offset from the world origin.
    // Undefined for collinear points, where the cross product is zero.
    CreateFromVertices(_: Plane, point1: Point3D, point2: Point3D, point3: Point3D): Plane
    {
        var n = point1.Between(point2).Cross(point1.Between(point3)).Normalize;
        return (Direction3D(n), point1.PositionVector.Dot(n));
    }

    // The dot product of the plane's four Hesse coefficients with a homogeneous
    // 4-vector. The fourth coefficient is -Distance, which is System.Numerics'
    // `D`, so this agrees with `Plane.Dot` there: for value = (p, 1) it is the
    // signed distance of p, and for value = (v, 0) the component of v along Normal.
    Dot(pl: Plane, value: Number4): Number
        => pl.Normal.Vector.X * value.X
         + pl.Normal.Vector.Y * value.Y
         + pl.Normal.Vector.Z * value.Z
         - pl.Distance * value.W;

    // The signed distance from a point to the plane, Dot(Normal, p) - Distance,
    // positive on the side the normal points to. The same quantity as
    // SignedDistance above, under the name the System.Numerics surface uses.
    DotCoordinate(pl: Plane, value: Point3D): Number
        => pl.SignedDistance(value);

    // The dot product of the plane's normal with a displacement: the component of
    // that displacement along the normal. Translation-invariant, so Distance plays
    // no part.
    DotNormal(pl: Plane, value: Vector3D): Number
        => value.Dot(pl.Normal.Vector);

    // The plane rotated by a quaternion. A rotation is rigid and fixes the origin,
    // so only the normal moves: the origin offset Distance is unchanged, and the
    // rotated normal is still unit.
    Transform(pl: Plane, rotation: Quaternion): Plane
        => (Direction3D(pl.Normal.Vector.Transform(rotation)), pl.Distance);

    // The plane carried through an arbitrary 4x4 transform. A plane is a covector,
    // so it transforms by the INVERSE TRANSPOSE of the point transform: with this
    // library's row-vector convention (v' = v M), the coefficient row
    // (Normal, -Distance) is multiplied by Transpose(Invert(matrix)). The result's
    // normal is NOT renormalized -- a non-uniform scale leaves it non-unit, which
    // breaks Direction3D's invariant until Normalize repairs it.
    Transform(pl: Plane, matrix: Matrix4x4): Plane
    {
        var m = matrix.Invert.Transpose;
        var n = pl.Normal.Vector;
        var q = Number4(n.X, n.Y, n.Z, -pl.Distance).Transform(m);
        return (Direction3D(Vector3D(q.X, q.Y, q.Z)), -q.W);
    }
